newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Lives of suspects threatened in key Sri Lanka case.
newsitem.headline: Lives of suspects threatened in key Sri Lanka case.

text.p: Three suspects held in last week's killing of a legislator from Sri Lanka's ruling coalition will not be present at their arraignment because of threats to their lives, their lawyer and police said on Wednesday.

The suspects, former mayor Mahinda Ratnatilleke and two police bodyguards of main opposition United National Party (UNP) legislator Susantha Punchinilame, were to be produced on Thursday before the magistrate of Ratnapura, 80 km (50 miles) southeast of Colombo, police said.
But an application to allow the suspects to be absent from the hearing had been upheld by authorities, Ratnatilleke's lawyer M.L.M. Ameen told Reuters.
"We asked that the suspects not be taken to Ratnapura due to the situation prevailing in the area," Ameen said. "Now there may be a proceeding without the suspects."
The three are among 11 suspects in custody in connection with last week's killing of ruling People's Alliance legislator Nalanda Ellawala.
The other eight suspects appeared in the Ratnapura court last week.
A senior officer with the police Criminal Investigation Department told Reuters the hearing for Ratnatilleke and the two policemen could be postponed.
Ratnatilleke, a UNP mayoral candidate in next month's local government polls, and the two policemen, a sergeant and a constable, surrendered to a magistrate in Colombo on Sunday and Tuesday.

Punchinilame, one of the main suspects, is still at large, police said. He is also a suspect in another murder case -- the 1989 killing of a student during a government crackdown on left-wing insurgents.
Suspects taken into custody have to be produced before a magistrate within seven days under emergency laws.
Ellawala, 29, was killed in a shootout between government supporters and rival UNP activists.
Ellawala's killing sparked riots in the gem mining town of Ratnapura as party activists burnt buildings and houses belonging to UNP supporters.
Rioters threw stones at the Ratnapura police station and damaged vehicles during the funeral last Saturday and threatened violence against the suspects.

Ellawala's killing came the day before the deadline for filing nominations for the March 21 local election, the first electoral contest between the UNP and the People's Alliance since it won the 1994 general election.
